 Judgment
This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the 3rd
respondent/insurer in O.P.(Mv) No.1060/2016 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Manjer
i, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the Award dated 14/10/2019.
The respondents herein are the claim petitioner and respondents 1 and 2 respectively in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 02/12/2014 at about 06:15 a.m., while he was riding a bicycle through the side of the road at the place by name Beemungal, motor cycle bearing registration no.KL-71/A-2514 ridden by the first respondent knocked down him casing grievous injuries.
The first respondent-rider and second respondent-owner remained ex parte.

sentences.text:
4. The third respondent/insurer filed written statement contending that the first respondent at the time of the accident was a minor and hence had no valid driving licence at the time of the accident and so the insurer has no liability.
5.
Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A6 series were marked on the side of the claimant/petitioner.
Exts.B1 and B2 were marked on the side of the third respondent.
Ext. X1
the disability certificate was also marked.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the 1st respondent-rider of the motor cycle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 4,00,500/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the 3rd respondent/insurer has come up 2025:KER:39833 in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.

It was submitted by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer that the finding of the Tribunal that there are no pleadings or proof regarding violation of the policy condition by the second respondent-owner of the offending motorbike is incorrect.
It was also pointed out that the failure to grant the relief of 'pay and recovery' is yet another infirmity committed by the Tribunal.
10. The Tribunal based on Ext.A3 final report/charge sheet concluded that the accident occurred due the rash and negligent driving of the first respondent-rider of the offending motorbike.
Ext.A1 copy of the FIR shows that the first respondent-rider of the offending bike was only 17 years at the time of the incident.

Therefore, it was argued before the Tribunal 2025:KER:39833 that it is quite apparent that the first respondent did not have any licence and hence the second respondent-owner has committed breach of the policy conditions and therefore the insurer is not liable to compensate the claim petitioner.

The Tribunal rejected the argument advanced on behalf of the third respondent/insurer and held that to avoid the liability under the policy, the insurer has to plead and prove that there was breach of the conditions in the policy.
The third respondent/insurer in the written statement denied the existence of a valid policy.
Hence the Tribunal concluded that there was no specific pleading regarding any breach of policy conditions.

The only evidence produced by the third respondent/insurer to prove breach of policy condition was Ext.B2 report, in which it is stated that the first respondent-rider was aged only 17 years at the time of the incident.
This according to the Tribunal was hardly sufficient to hold that he had no licence and that there was breach of policy conditions.
It was noticed that there was no mention in Ext.A3 charge sheet regarding the fact that the first respondent had no valid driving licence.
The 2025:KER:39833 Tribunal also took note of the proviso to Sub-section (1) of Section 4 of the Act, which permits a person who attained the age of 16 years to drive certain type of motorcycles.

The Tribunal found the materials on record insufficient to prove breach of policy conditions and hence it was held that the third respondent could not be absolved from the liability to indemnify the second M/S.United India Insurance Company ... vs Mohammed Sinan on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54171513/
3 respondent/insured.

sentences.text: As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the third respondent/insurer, Ext.B1 policy shows that the motorcycle that was insured had an engine capacity of 150 CC.
Apparently, proviso to Sub-section (1) of Section 4 of the Act would not be attracted in this case.

That being the position,
the rider of the offending bike did require a licence to ride the same.
In the written statement, the third respondent has contended that the first respondent/rider did not have a valid driving licence at the time of the incident.
As per Section 149 (2)(a)(ii) of the Act, absence of a valid driving licence is one of the defences that can be taken up by the insurer in a claim petition.
Before the 2025:KER:39833 Tribunal, the first respondent rider of the offending motorbike and the second respondent-owner/insured remained ex-parte.
Ext.B2 proves that the first respondent was only 17 years at the time of the incident and had no valid driving licence to ride the vehicle.
Hence, there is a breach of a policy condition.

But as held in National Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Swaran Singh, (2004) 3 SCC 297 and by a Larger Bench of this Court in Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. v. Paulose, 2015 (1) KLT 682, though there is a breach of the policy condition, the third respondent/insurer shall pay and will have the right to recover the same from the second respondent-owner/insured.

sentences.text: 12. In the appeal memorandum, though it is alleged that the compensation that has been awarded by the Tribunal under various heads is excessive, on going through the impugned Award, I do not find any grounds for interference.
In the result, the appeal is allowed in part.
The impugned Award is confirmed.
The third respondent/insurer shall pay the amount to the claim petitioner and thereafter recover it from the 2025:KER:39833 second respondent-owner/insured.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
